artiest/walter-gieseking.text:
Walter Gieseking was born in Lyon in 1895, the son of a German doctor, and grew up to be a German pianist. He began playing the piano at the age of four without any formal lessons, and from 1911 to 1916 he studied at the conservatory in Hanover with Karl Leimer, with whom he later wrote a piano method. He gave his first concert in 1915, and his first recital in London in 1923 established his reputation. He had an exceptional memory and often learned new repertoire away from the piano, on the train.

Gieseking is known for his subtle touch, his pedalling and his command of dynamics, above all in the music of Debussy and Ravel. He recorded virtually all the piano music of those two composers, as well as most of Mozart's solo works. In 1944 he played Beethoven's Emperor Concerto in a recording on which anti-aircraft fire can be heard, one of the earliest stereo recordings. His repertoire ranged from Bach and Beethoven to Rachmaninoff, Hindemith and Schoenberg. He also composed music himself, which he barely made public.

During the war he continued to perform in Germany and was accused of Nazi sympathies. After the war he was briefly blacklisted. In 1947 he was cleared by the American military government, but an American tour in 1949 was cancelled after protests. He died in London in 1956, while recording all of the Beethoven sonatas. He also collected butterflies. Gieseking is regarded as the pianist who gave the French Impressionists a clear, transparent sound.
artiest/walter-gieseking.listen: Listen to an extract from his recording of Debussy's Préludes and notice the soft touch and the care for dynamics. Can you hear how each note seems to arise almost without the sound of a hammer?

artiest/walter-maioli.text:
Walter Maioli is an Italian researcher, multi-instrumentalist and composer, born in Milan in 1950. He specialised in experimental archaeology and music, particularly that of archaic civilisations, and has spent more than thirty-five years studying the music of antiquity and prehistory. From the early 1970s he travelled around the Mediterranean and became familiar with Arabic, African, Eastern and European music. In 1972 he founded Aktuala, a pioneer of world music that focused on African and Asian folk music.

In the 1980s his attention turned to prehistoric instruments. Albums from this period include Amazonia 6891 and Ethnoelectronics, both from 1986, on which jungle sounds, natural objects, echo and electronics come together. In 1991 he showed a collection on the origins of musical instruments at the Natural History Museum in Milan and, with Fiorella Terenzi, made sounds for the planetarium. From 1994 he coordinated the music of the Archeon archaeological theme park in Alphen aan den Rijn, which resulted in the CD Archeon 200000 Jaar Muziek.

In 1995 he founded Synaulia, a group of musicians, archaeologists and dancers who perform ancient Etruscan and Roman music and dance, including at archaeological sites in Italy. For the 1998 film A Midsummer Night's Dream he provided the reconstructed instruments. Two songs by Synaulia were used in Gladiator, and the group made music for, among others, the BBC and HBO series Rome. In this way Maioli links the world music of the 1970s with an attempt to hear how antiquity sounded.
artiest/walter-maioli.listen: Listen to an extract from the album Amazonia 6891 and notice how the sounds of nature and the electronic sounds alternate. Can you hear where the sound comes from nature and where from the machine?

artiest/walter-page.text:
Walter Page was born in Gallatin, Missouri, in 1900 and grew up in Kansas City. At Lincoln High School he learned the double bass from the former military bandleader Major N. Clark Smith, after first playing bass drum and bass horn in brass bands. He studied at the University of Kansas and, between 1918 and 1923, played tuba, bass saxophone and double bass in Bennie Moten's orchestra. In 1925 he formed Walter Page and the Blue Devils, a territory band from the area around Oklahoma City and Wichita, in which Count Basie, Jimmy Rushing and Lester Young, among others, played.

Page drew attention above all with his bass playing. He is regarded as one of the first to play four beats to the bar and as the most important spreader of the walking bass, in place of the older two-beat style of New Orleans. His sound was so solid that Eddie Durham said he was like a house with one note. He played in Count Basie's orchestra from 1935 to 1942 and again from 1946 to 1949. Together with the pianist Basie, the drummer Jo Jones and the guitarist Freddie Green, he formed the All-American Rhythm Section, the rhythm section that defined the Basie sound. He left room for the soloists and played a straight line.

Page also played baritone saxophone and tuba, and with the Kansas City Six he recorded one of the first jazz solos on double bass, Pagin' the Devil. Later he worked as a freelancer with, among others, Buck Clayton, Roy Eldridge and Eddie Condon. He died in New York in 1957 of pneumonia. Because of his early death he remains less well known than his influence deserves, for his walking bass became the model for later jazz bassists.
artiest/walter-page.listen: Listen to a Count Basie recording from the 1930s and notice the bass in the rhythm section. Can you hear how four even beats to the bar carry the whole orchestra?

artiest/walter-page-s-blue-devils.text:
Walter Page's Blue Devils was a territory band, an orchestra that toured its own region, in this case the area around Oklahoma City and Wichita in Kansas. The bassist Walter Page founded the group in 1925, after Billy King's Road Show, with which he had toured the United States, had broken up. That road show already featured the later Basie musicians Jimmy Rushing and Count Basie. The band lasted six years, from 1925 to 1931. Page led it from behind the bass and also played baritone saxophone. His nickname was Big 'Un.

Over the years the band included names that would later shape jazz: Count Basie, Jimmy Rushing, Buster Smith, Lester Young and Hot Lips Page. Only two recording sessions of the group exist. In 1929 it recorded a handful of numbers in Kansas City for Vocalion, including Blue Devil Blues. On it Page plays first tuba, then double bass and finally baritone saxophone.

Page was eager to measure his band against the orchestra of Bennie Moten from Kansas City. Moten avoided a direct contest and preferred to buy away individual musicians with high wages. Basie and Eddie Durham left in 1929, shortly afterwards Rushing, and eventually Page himself. Beset by money worries, booking problems and a conflict with the musicians' union, he had to hand over the leadership to others. Page then played with Moten and later with Basie. The Blue Devils show how the swing of Kansas City grew out of touring orchestras in the Southwest, full of riffs and a solid rhythm.
artiest/walter-page-s-blue-devils.listen: Listen to Blue Devil Blues from 1929 and notice the bass. Can you hear the switch between tuba, double bass and baritone saxophone, all played by Walter Page?

artiest/wanda-jackson.text:
Wanda Jackson was born in Maud, Oklahoma, in 1937 and grew up in Oklahoma City. Her father taught her to play the guitar, and as a teenager she got her own radio show. The country singer Hank Thompson heard her and in 1954 helped her get a contract with Decca. Her first hit was the duet You Can't Have My Love. In 1955 she toured with Elvis Presley, who encouraged her to sing rock 'n' roll. In 1956 she signed with Capitol, where the producer Ken Nelson allowed her the freedom to record both country and rockabilly.

At Capitol she made rock songs such as Fujiyama Mama, Mean Mean Man and Baby Loves Him, often with country on one side of the single and rockabilly on the other. Critics call those records sexually daring and almost wild. Fujiyama Mama reached number one in Japan in 1958, and Let's Have a Party made the American Hot 100 in 1960. Her nickname became the Queen of Rockabilly. In the 1960s she leaned more towards country and also recorded German-language records, of which Santo Domingo topped the charts in Austria in 1965.

After 1971 gospel was at the centre of her career. From 1984 she returned to rock 'n' roll, among other things through Rosie Flores in 1995 and the 2003 album Heart Trouble. In 2009 she was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. With Jack White she made The Party Ain't Over in 2011. In 2019 she bade farewell to performing. Jackson was one of the first women to have a career in rock 'n' roll and showed that a girl with a guitar could match the boys.
artiest/wanda-jackson.listen: Listen to Let's Have a Party and notice her raw, screaming voice over the boogie piano and the guitar. Can you hear how she fires up the party herself?

artiest/wardell-gray.text:
Wardell Gray was born in Oklahoma City in 1921 and grew up in Detroit. He started on clarinet but switched to tenor saxophone after hearing Lester Young with Count Basie's orchestra. At the end of 1943 he joined Earl Hines's orchestra, at first on alto saxophone. Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker had played in that orchestra before him. At the end of 1946 he settled in Los Angeles and recorded his first session under his own name there, with Dodo Marmarosa on piano.

In the clubs on Central Avenue Gray fought tenor duels with Dexter Gordon. The label boss Ross Russell had them record one such duel as The Chase, Gray's first nationally known recording, which has also been called one of the most exciting musical contests in jazz. After that he played with Benny Goodman and with Count Basie, including in his septet of 1950 and 1951. He wrote Twisted, on which Annie Ross later based a successful vocalese version. His playing was fluid and clear, full of ideas.

Gray got involved with drugs in the 1950s, recorded less and played with less fire. In May 1955, after a performance in Las Vegas, he was found dead in the desert, aged 34. The cause of death was an overdose. He is regarded, after Dexter Gordon, as one of the finest tenor saxophonists of the bop era, influenced by Lester Young and a forerunner of Stan Getz. Jack Kerouac mentions him in On the Road.
artiest/wardell-gray.listen: Listen to The Chase by Wardell Gray and Dexter Gordon and notice how the two tenor saxophonists trade phrases and try to outdo each other. Who plays when, and can you hear the difference in tone?

artiest/warne-marsh.text:
Warne Marsh was born in Los Angeles in 1927 into an artistic family: his father was a cameraman in Hollywood and his mother a violinist. He began on alto saxophone but soon switched to tenor. During his military service he heard about the blind pianist Lennie Tristano in New York. He made contact, took lessons and played in Tristano's group. In March 1949 he made his first recordings with Tristano and Lee Konitz, including the record Crosscurrent.

Marsh remained faithful to Tristano's teaching: the pure long line, no stock phrases and no cheap emotion, and endless work on a limited number of standards. His playing generally sounded cool, with subtly displaced rhythms that are instantly recognisable. He belonged to Cool Jazz and often stood in Konitz's shadow. His best-known record from that period is Lee Konitz with Warne Marsh from 1955, on which they improvise together. After that he withdrew for years and did not make an album under his own name again until 1969. Anthony Braxton called him the greatest vertical improviser.

In the 1970s Marsh received renewed attention as a member of Supersax, a large ensemble that played Charlie Parker's solos in orchestral arrangements. He died in 1987 of a heart attack on the stage of the club Donte's in Los Angeles, in the middle of Out of Nowhere. He remains an insider's tip among jazz musicians, and younger players such as Mark Turner draw inspiration from his music.
artiest/warne-marsh.listen: Listen to Lee Konitz with Warne Marsh and notice how the tenor and the alto saxophone improvise together in long, winding lines. Can you hear how little vibrato and effect Marsh uses?

artiest/warren-ellis.text:
Warren Ellis is an Australian musician and composer, born in Ballarat, Victoria, in 1965. By his own account he came to music by chance: on the rubbish dump he found an abandoned accordion, which he took to school. Later he learned classical violin and flute and studied violin in Melbourne. In 1988 he travelled through Europe, playing as a street musician. After his return he wrote music for theatre groups and played in bands. In 1992 he founded the Dirty Three with the guitarist Mick Turner and the drummer Jim White.

In 1993 he was asked to join a small string group on Let Love In, the 1994 album by Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds. He soon became a permanent member, at first on violin, later on many more instruments, including piano, accordion, bouzouki, guitar, flute and mandolin. He co-wrote many of the band's songs and played in Grinderman, a side project of the Bad Seeds. In 2002 his solo album Three Pieces for Violin was released.

With Nick Cave, Ellis made film music for, among others, The Proposition from 2005, The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford, The Road, Lawless and Hell or High Water. Without Cave he wrote, among other things, the music for Mustang. He has lived in Paris since 1998. Ellis shows that a violinist from a rock band can carry a film score with few notes, plenty of atmosphere and a raw, often repeated sound.
artiest/warren-ellis.listen: Listen to a piece from The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford and notice the violin and the slow, repeated piano notes. Can you hear how few instruments it takes to create a tense atmosphere?

artiest/waylon.text:
Waylon is the stage name of Willem Bijkerk, a Dutch singer, born in Apeldoorn in 1980. He named himself after his idol Waylon Jennings. As a child he was inspired by country music, played drums in the band West Virginian Railroad and sang along in the TV programme Telekids. In 1997 he signed with EMI and was allowed to record an album in Nashville, which never came out. In 2001 he lived and worked in the United States for a year and performed with Waylon Jennings.

His breakthrough came in 2008 with the first season of Holland's Got Talent, where he reached the final with It's a Man's Man's Man's World by James Brown. Universal signed him as the first Dutchman on the Motown label. His debut album Wicked Ways was released in 2009, with the single Wicked Way. In 2010 he won a 3FM Award for best newcomer. After that came After All in 2011 and Heaven After Midnight in 2014, which topped the Dutch album chart.

In 2014 he formed the duo The Common Linnets with Ilse DeLange. With the country and bluegrass song Calm After the Storm they came second at the Eurovision Song Contest in Copenhagen. Waylon left the group after a concert in June of that year. In 2016 Seeds was released, an album in every style with the disco single Our Song, and in 2018 he entered the Eurovision Song Contest as a soloist with Outlaw in 'Em. He has also been a coach on television programmes such as The Voice of Holland. Waylon brought Nashville country to a broad Dutch audience.
artiest/waylon.listen: Listen to Calm After the Storm by The Common Linnets and notice the harmony singing of two voices above the acoustic guitars. Can you hear how the voices alternate and then carry on together?

artiest/wayne-shorter.text: The saxophonist Wayne Shorter, from Newark, played in Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers from 1959 to 1964, where he also became musical director. In his early playing you can hear the influence of Sonny Rollins and John Coltrane. In 1964 he joined Miles Davis's second quintet, for which he wrote pieces such as E.S.P., Footprints and Nefertiti. For Blue Note he made albums such as Speak No Evil and Juju, with enigmatic melodies and unusual harmonies. In 1970 he founded Weather Report with Joe Zawinul. Later he led an acoustic quartet well into old age. Shorter is regarded as one of the most important composers in jazz.
artiest/wayne-shorter.listen: Listen to the theme: it sounds simple, but the chords underneath keep heading in a different direction.

artiest/wayne-smith.text:
Wayne Smith was born Ian Flemmings Smith in 1965 and grew up in Waterhouse, a district of Kingston, Jamaica. He performed at sound systems and began recording in 1980, at the age of fourteen. In the beginning he worked with the producer Prince Jammy, his neighbour, who produced his debut album Youthman Skanking and, in 1985, its follow-up Smoker Super. His early style was rooted in roots reggae, but slowed down, in the spacious dancehall style of the time, with backing from, among others, the Roots Radics, with Scientist and King Tubby at the controls.

In 1985 he recorded Under Mi Sleng Teng, the song that is seen as the start of the digital age of reggae. The rhythm part came from a preset pattern on a Casio MT-40, not from real musicians. The lyrics were inspired by Under Mi Sensi by Barrington Levy. There are several stories about who discovered the pattern, but usually Smith and Noel Davey are named. He went on to have further hits with Come Along and Ain't No Meaning in Saying Goodbye. In 1989 he moved to New York and started his own label, Sleng Teng Records. He died in 2014.

The step from real instruments to digital rhythms had major consequences, for ragga and later for jungle, rave and drum and bass. That makes this one song a turning point in the history of dance music.
artiest/wayne-smith.listen: Listen to Under Mi Sleng Teng and notice the angular, electronic beat and the low bass line. Note that there is no real drummer and no real bass player to be heard.

artiest/weather-report.text:
Weather Report was an American jazz rock band, founded in 1970 by the Austrian keyboard player Joe Zawinul, the American saxophonist Wayne Shorter and the Czech bassist Miroslav Vitouš. Zawinul and Shorter had known each other since 1959 from Maynard Ferguson's big band. Both played on the groundbreaking Miles Davis albums In a Silent Way and Bitches Brew. With their own band they wanted to get away from the fixed forms of jazz, in which a theme is followed by solos in turn.

The first records, such as Weather Report (1971) and I Sing the Body Electric (1972), were free and experimental, with a lot of group improvisation. From Sweetnighter (1973) Zawinul steered the band towards funk and groove, with influences from rhythm and blues and from music from other parts of the world. Vitouš left, and after Alphonso Johnson the bassist Jaco Pastorius joined in 1976. With him the music became more melodic and the band reached a large audience. Heavy Weather (1977), with Zawinul's song Birdland, became their best-known record. In 1986 Weather Report came to an end.

Alongside Mahavishnu Orchestra, Return to Forever and Herbie Hancock's Headhunters, Weather Report was regarded as one of the defining bands of jazz rock. Zawinul always used the latest synthesizers and searched for new timbres. Shorter played with restraint and attentive listening, and Pastorius made the fretless bass guitar popular as a melodic instrument. In this way the band built on what Miles Davis had begun with Bitches Brew.
artiest/weather-report.listen: Listen to Birdland and notice how the theme is built up step by step, from a simple motif to a large, festive chorus. Hear how synthesizer, saxophone and bass take turns carrying the melody.

artiest/webb-pierce.text:
Webb Pierce was born in West Monroe, Louisiana, in 1921. As a child he listened to records by Jimmie Rodgers and to western swing and Cajun music, and at fifteen he got his own radio show. He performed in Shreveport and joined the Louisiana Hayride. There he put together a group of local musicians that included, among others, the pianist Floyd Cramer and the guitarist and singer Faron Young. In 1951 he signed with Decca. His second single, Wondering, became his first number one on the country chart in 1952.

In September 1952 he took a place in the Grand Ole Opry, vacated after the dismissal of Hank Williams. After Williams's death Pierce became the most popular country singer. His hits include There Stands the Glass from 1953, Slowly from 1954, More and More from 1954 and In the Jailhouse Now from 1955, which stayed at number one for 21 weeks. Slowly was the first successful record to feature a pedal steel guitar. His voice was described as a whining, whiskey-tinged tenor full of emotion. In the 1950s he had more number one hits than any other country artist. He also sang duets with Kitty Wells and in 1958 recorded a rockabilly record under the name Shady Wall.

Pierce was notorious for his extravagant lifestyle, with flashy Nudie suits, two convertibles with silver dollars set into the upholstery and a guitar-shaped swimming pool. He went on making records until 1982, including a duet with Willie Nelson of In the Jailhouse Now. He died in 1991 and was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2001. Pierce was the face of the honky-tonk of the 1950s, just before the arrival of rock 'n' roll.
artiest/webb-pierce.listen: Listen to In the Jailhouse Now and notice the high, whining tenor voice. Can you hear how the voice is up front, with the band behind it?

artiest/weezer.text:
Weezer is an American rock band from Los Angeles, formed in February 1992 by the singer and guitarist Rivers Cuomo, the drummer Patrick Wilson, the bassist Matt Sharp and the guitarist Jason Cropper. Cuomo had come to Los Angeles from Connecticut with a metal band, but then became captivated by alternative rock such as Nirvana, the Pixies and Sonic Youth. The name came from a nickname his father gave him. In 1993 the band signed with Geffen Records. During the recording of the first album Brian Bell took Cropper's place.

The debut Weezer (1994), known as the Blue Album, was produced by Ric Ocasek of The Cars and was a great success, with the singles Buddy Holly and Say It Ain't So. The music videos by Spike Jonze helped; for Buddy Holly he edited the band into footage from the television series Happy Days. The second album, Pinkerton (1996), sounded darker and rawer and flopped, but later grew into a cult record. After a break the band returned in 2001 with the Green Album and Island in the Sun. Since then Weezer has released many more albums, several of which are again simply called Weezer, with a different coloured sleeve.

Weezer combined alternative rock with power pop: heavily distorted guitars, but also catchy melodies and multi-part vocals. The lyrics were full of nerd humour and references to popular culture. Pinkerton is cited as an influence on many emo bands of the 2000s.
artiest/weezer.listen: Listen to Buddy Holly and notice the contrast: the melody and the backing vocals sound like cheerful 1950s pop, but the guitars are thick and distorted. Hear how that makes the chorus sound sweet and loud at the same time.

artiest/wendy-carlos.text: Wendy Carlos studied music and physics and advised Robert Moog on the development of his synthesizer. Her album Switched-On Bach (1968), Bach's music played on the Moog, was a worldwide success. With the producer Rachel Elkind she wrote the music for Stanley Kubrick's A Clockwork Orange (1971). It features synthesizer versions of Purcell and Beethoven as well as original pieces. For The Shining (1980) they reworked the old Gregorian Dies irae melody into a menacing title piece. For Tron (1982) Carlos combined synthesizer with symphony orchestra. She showed that the synthesizer could be a serious instrument for film music.
artiest/wendy-carlos.listen: Notice the synthesizer sound that imitates and distorts old, familiar music, such as the Dies irae melody in The Shining.

artiest/wendy-carlos-en-rachel-elkind.text:
Wendy Carlos was born in Rhode Island in 1939 and studied physics and music at Brown University. In 1962 she then went to Columbia University in New York to study composition, where she worked at the Columbia-Princeton Electronic Music Center with pioneers such as Vladimir Ussachevsky and Otto Luening. She helped Robert Moog develop the Moog synthesizer and gave a great deal of advice on the keyboard and other components. In 1967 she met Rachel Elkind, a former singer who worked at the same recording studio. The two became friends and shared a house, a studio and a business.

Together they made Switched-On Bach, released in 1968: music by Johann Sebastian Bach, played on a Moog synthesizer. Carlos had actually wanted to make an album of her own music, but Elkind suggested familiar music. The record won three Grammys and made the synthesizer popular in the 1970s. Later Carlos wrote the film music for A Clockwork Orange in 1971, The Shining in 1980 and Tron in 1982. Main Title from The Shining features in this list.

Carlos shows that electronic sounds need not be cold. Her synthesizer work opened the way to electronic film music and synth-pop. In 1979 she made public that she had been living as a woman since 1968.
artiest/wendy-carlos-en-rachel-elkind.listen: Listen to Main Title and notice the low, menacing electronic sounds. Can you hear how the synthesizer builds a feeling of unease before anything has even happened?

artiest/wes-montgomery.text:
Wes Montgomery was born in Indianapolis in 1923 and for years worked as a welder and machinist. He did not start playing the guitar seriously until he was nineteen, after hearing a record by Charlie Christian, and he learned to play by copying Christian's solos. In 1948 Lionel Hampton took him into his band, but he did not enjoy touring and returned to Indianapolis. There he played with his brothers Buddy and Monk and with the organist Melvin Rhyne. The saxophonist Cannonball Adderley heard him in a club and got him a deal with Riverside, where his first album as a leader came out in 1959.

Montgomery played without a pick: he struck the strings with the side of his thumb, at first so as not to wake his neighbours and children at night. This gave him a warm, round sound. His trademark was playing in octaves. He often built a solo in three layers: first single notes, then octaves and finally full chords. On albums such as The Incredible Jazz Guitar of Wes Montgomery from 1960 and Full House he played hard bop and soul jazz.

In 1964 he moved to Verve, where the producer Creed Taylor mainly had him make instrumental versions of pop songs, such as California Dreamin' and Windy. Those records were his greatest commercial successes, and Goin' Out of My Head earned a Grammy. Montgomery died of a heart attack in 1968, aged 45. His octave technique and his warm sound influenced, among others, George Benson and later fusion and smooth jazz.
artiest/wes-montgomery.listen: Listen to Windy and notice the guitar melody played in octaves. Can you hear how the two notes together form a single warm line, without the sharp attack of a pick?

artiest/wessel-ilcken.text:
Wessel Ilcken was a Dutch jazz drummer, born in Hilversum in 1923. His mother gave him a drum kit and he taught himself the instrument for the most part. He was influenced by Jo Jones, the drummer of Count Basie's orchestra. During the war the German occupiers banned jazz, but Ilcken played in Piet van Dijk's orchestra. There he met the singer Rita Reys, whom he married in 1945. At first he went along on her travels as her husband, but he took a seat behind the drum kit when the drummer fell ill.

The couple performed in North Africa and in Great Britain and in 1950 settled in Stockholm, an important European jazz centre with musicians such as Arne Domnérus and Lars Gullin. Back in the Netherlands, from 1954, they played as Rita Reys and the Wessel Ilcken Combo, including at the Amsterdam club Scheherazade. Ilcken worked on records and on stage with Americans such as Dizzy Gillespie, Stan Kenton, Herbie Mann, Joe Carroll and Bob Cooper. He played on the albums Jazz Behind the Dikes from 1955 and 1956.

Ilcken was also a good water-skier and in May 1957 became the first Dutch champion. Shortly afterwards he died, aged 33, of a cerebral haemorrhage. His name lives on in the Wessel Ilcken Prize for Dutch jazz musicians, which was established in 1963 and later became the Boy Edgar Prize. He was regarded as a central figure of Dutch jazz in the age of bebop.
artiest/wessel-ilcken.listen: Listen to a recording of Rita Reys with Wessel Ilcken and notice the drumming beneath the vocals. Can you hear how the drummer gives the singer room and yet carries the rhythm?

artiest/westminster-cathedral-choir-en-d.text:
The Westminster Cathedral Choir is the choir of Westminster Cathedral in London, the largest Catholic church in England and Wales and the seat of the Archbishop of Westminster. The cathedral was built between 1895 and 1903 in a Neo-Byzantine style, almost entirely of brick. Its large, resonant space forms the choir's natural sounding board. David Hill is the conductor who led the choir in the twentieth century and with whom the recordings in the course are associated.

The choir is known for performing Renaissance polyphony in the liturgy, including that of the Spanish composer Tomás Luis de Victoria. His motet O magnum mysterium from 1572 is one of the best-known examples. Several voices sing in and around one another, without instruments, in long, flowing lines.

For the history of pop, such choral music is both a source and a counterweight: it shows how singing can sound in a church space and how much power a voice has without accompaniment. Many later artists have used that sound to evoke atmosphere and awe.
artiest/westminster-cathedral-choir-en-d.listen: Listen to O magnum mysterium and notice how the voices enter one after another and the reverberation of the church lets their sound ring on. Try to follow a single voice.

artiest/wham.text:
Wham! was an English pop duo from Bushey, formed in 1981 by George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley. The two met at school in 1975 and first played in a short-lived ska band, The Executive. They then formed Wham!, a name which, according to Ridgeley, was meant to capture their energy and friendship. The exclamation mark was added by a British design agency. They signed with Innervision Records, and the debut album Fantastic was released in 1983. It was about unemployment and young people's fear of growing up.

The second album, Make It Big, from 1984, reached number one in both England and the United States. Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go, Careless Whisper and Everything She Wants each reached the top of the American Hot 100. Last Christmas from 1984 became a permanent Christmas classic, and the proceeds went to charity. In 1985 the group became the first Western pop group to make a ten-day visit to China, which was seen as a milestone in relations between China and the West.

The music was influenced by funk and soul. In their early period Wham! presented themselves as bored young men and appealed mainly to a young audience. In 1986 the duo split up, because Michael wanted to make music for a more mature audience. There followed the farewell single The Edge of Heaven, the compilation album The Final and a farewell concert. In the series on youth cultures, Wham! shows how a youth band of the 1980s became a worldwide success.
artiest/wham.listen: Listen to Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go. Notice the cheerful beat, in which funk and soul can be heard, and how the two voices alternate.

artiest/white-noise.text:
White Noise was a British experimental electronic group, founded in London in 1968 by David Vorhaus. He was an American-born classical bassist with a background in physics and electronics, and he set to work on the project after attending a lecture by Delia Derbyshire of the BBC Radiophonic Workshop. Derbyshire and Brian Hodgson joined him.

In 1969 the album An Electric Storm was released on Island Records. It was made using tape manipulation and the EMS Synthi VCS3, the first British synthesizer. The opening track, Love Without Sound, uses sped-up recordings of Vorhaus on the double bass to create violin and cello sounds. The album at first sold poorly, but is now considered important for the development of electronic music. Groups such as The Orb and Broadcast cite it as an inspiration. After Derbyshire and Hodgson left, Vorhaus carried on: White Noise 2 appeared in 1974, followed by Re-Entry in 1980, and Inferno and Sound Mind in 2000. For the fiftieth anniversary of the debut, Lightning Strikes Twice was released in 2021.

White Noise shows that the studio itself could be an instrument. In doing so the group opened the way for later electronic pop music and ambient.
artiest/white-noise.listen: Listen to Love Without Sound and notice the string-like sounds. These are not real violins and cellos, but processed double bass sounds. Can you hear how strange and yet soft that sounds?

artiest/whitesnake.text:
Whitesnake was a British rock band, formed in London in 1978. The group began as the backing band of the singer David Coverdale, who had left Deep Purple shortly before. Coverdale remained the only constant member. After the Snakebite EP in 1978 came the albums Trouble in 1978 and Lovehunter in 1979, with live favourites such as Ain't No Love in the Heart of the City and Walking in the Shadow of the Blues. With Ready an' Willing, Come an' Get It and Saints & Sinners the band reached the top ten in England, Europe and Japan.

In the mid-1980s Coverdale turned his attention to the American market, where Whitesnake was still unknown. With the support of Geffen Records, Slide It In came out in 1984, with singles that got heavy airplay on MTV. In 1987 came the album Whitesnake, called 1987 in England, with the hits Here I Go Again, Is This Love and Still of the Night. The band took on a newer look, closer to the glam metal of Los Angeles. After Slip of the Tongue in 1989 Coverdale took a break. Around 2003 he put together a new line-up, and in 2025 he announced that he was stopping.

The band's early sound is called blues rock. Later it shifted towards more accessible hard rock. The lyrics are often about love and sex, with a great deal of innuendo. Whitesnake features on lists of the best hard rock bands. In the story of Nederpop the group has a Dutch side, because Adrian Vandenberg joined as guitarist in 1987.
artiest/whitesnake.listen: Listen to Here I Go Again by Whitesnake. Notice the heavy guitars and the chorus, and how Coverdale's singing makes the song sound more like hard rock than blues.

artiest/whitney-houston.text:
Whitney Houston was born in Newark, New Jersey, in 1963, the daughter of the gospel and soul singer Cissy Houston. Dionne Warwick was her cousin. From the age of five she sang in the choir of the New Hope Baptist Church, and her mother taught her to sing. As a teenager she sang in her mother's band and as a backing singer for, among others, Chaka Khan and Lou Rawls. She also worked as a fashion model and was one of the first Black women on the cover of the magazine Seventeen. In 1983 she signed with Arista Records, where Clive Davis took his time to find the right material for her.

Her debut album Whitney Houston was released in 1985 and produced hits such as Saving All My Love for You, How Will I Know and Greatest Love of All. The second album, Whitney (1987), opened with I Wanna Dance with Somebody (Who Loves Me), and with it she had seven consecutive number one hits in America. In the 1990s she appeared in films such as The Bodyguard (1992), with I Will Always Love You. Drug use and a difficult marriage overshadowed her later years. She died in Beverly Hills in 2012.

Houston was called The Voice: a powerful, clear voice, formed in the church, which she deployed in polished pop and ballads. She broke barriers for Black artists; the video for How Will I Know was played often on MTV, when that channel still showed few Black artists. In this way she brought the vocal art of gospel to the biggest stages of pop.
artiest/whitney-houston.listen: Listen to I Wanna Dance with Somebody and notice the contrast between the cheerful synthesizers and drum machine and Houston's voice. Hear how, towards the end, she adds more and more embellishments and flourishes, like a gospel singer in church.

artiest/wiener-johann-strauss-orchester.text:
The Wiener Johann Strauss Orchester is an Austrian orchestra from Vienna. It was founded in 1966 under the direction of Professor Oskar Goger and with the support of the Austrian broadcaster ORF. Its first conductor was Eduard Strauss II, a nephew of Johann Strauss III, who continued the musical tradition of the Strauss family in the twentieth century.

The aim of the orchestra was to emulate the travelling Strauss orchestra of the time of Johann Strauss I, the founder of the dynasty. The musicians came from the best Viennese orchestras, such as the Wiener Symphoniker and the Vienna radio orchestra, so that the quality would be high. In October 1966 Eduard Strauss II took the orchestra on tour through North America, which was a great success. He remained associated with the orchestra until his death in 1969.

Afterwards Willi Boskovsky became principal conductor. With him the orchestra recorded a large part of the music of the Strauss family for the EMI label, on albums such as The Magic of Vienna and Strauss, Willi Boskovsky Conducts Lehár Waltzes and Kaiser-Walzer. Later the orchestra was conducted by, among others, Franz Bauer-Theussl, Alfred Eschwé and Martin Sieghart, and Johannes Wildner has led the concert in the Musikverein on the Austrian national holiday since 2008. The orchestra preserves the Viennese waltz tradition as light, danceable concert music and made it known on record.
artiest/wiener-johann-strauss-orchester.listen: Listen to Kaiser-Walzer and notice the typically Viennese waltz rhythm, with a slight delay on the second beat. Can you hear how the orchestra makes the dance sway?

artiest/wiener-philharmoniker.text:
The Wiener Philharmoniker is a Viennese symphony orchestra that was founded in 1842 and is counted among the best in the world. The orchestra is based in the Musikverein in Vienna and consists of musicians from the Staatsoper orchestra. The orchestra is self-governing and takes its decisions by democratic vote. The first concerts were conducted by Otto Nicolai, and in 1860 the series of subscription concerts began that continues to this day. In 1870 the orchestra moved to the Goldener Saal of the Musikverein, whose acoustics define its sound.

The list of conductors is long. Under Hans Richter the orchestra gave the first performances of Brahms's Second and Third Symphonies and of Bruckner's Eighth. Gustav Mahler led it from 1898 to 1901, and later Felix Weingartner, Wilhelm Furtwängler, Bruno Walter, Herbert von Karajan, Karl Böhm and Leonard Bernstein, among others, worked with the Philharmoniker. Carlos Kleiber appeared with the orchestra thirty times between 1974 and 1994. In 2000 the orchestra played Beethoven's Ninth on the site of the Mauthausen concentration camp, without a fee and without applause.

Since 1 January 1941 the orchestra has given the New Year's Concert every New Year's Day, with music by the Strauss family, above all Johann Strauss II. The orchestra has made many recordings, such as Das Lied von der Erde in 1952 and Tchaikovsky's Pathétique. The Philharmoniker are not obliged to hire musicians over the age of 35, and members retire at sixty-five. In this way the Wiener Philharmoniker preserves a Viennese playing style of its own.
artiest/wiener-philharmoniker.listen: Listen to a recording of the New Year's Concert and notice the strings in the waltz. Can you hear how the orchestra holds back the second beat of the waltz by a fraction?

artiest/wiener-staatsoper.text:
The Wiener Staatsoper is the opera house and the opera company of Vienna. The Neo-Renaissance building was constructed between 1861 and 1869 to plans by August Sicard von Sicardsburg and Eduard van der Nüll, as the first major building on the Wiener Ringstrasse. It opened as the Hofoper, in the presence of Emperor Franz Joseph, with Mozart's Don Giovanni on 25 May 1869. The house received its present name after the founding of the First Republic in 1921. The members of the Wiener Philharmoniker are drawn from the Staatsoper orchestra.

Gustav Mahler was director here from 1897 to 1907. He trained a new generation of singers, had economical, modern sets made and introduced the dimming of the lights during the performance. On 12 March 1945 the house caught fire in an American bombing raid, in which the auditorium, the stage and almost all the sets and costumes were lost. The front section with the foyer and staircases remained standing. In the meantime the company played at the Theater an der Wien and the Volksoper.

On 5 November 1955 the rebuilt house was reopened with Beethoven's Fidelio under Karl Böhm, in the first live broadcast by the Austrian broadcaster ORF. After the war the conductor Josef Krips built up the Mozart ensemble, which sought a clearer, lighter sound that later came to be called typically Viennese. The house records its performances on albums such as Così fan tutte, Salome and Die Walküre. Every year the Staatsoper also organises the Vienna Opera Ball.
artiest/wiener-staatsoper.listen: Listen to a recording of Così fan tutte from the Staatsoper and notice the singers blending in the ensembles. Can you hear how the voices alternate and complement one another?

artiest/wild-romance.text:
Wild Romance, also known as Herman Brood & His Wild Romance, was the backing band of the Dutch singer and pianist Herman Brood. The group was formed in Groningen in 1976 and went through changing line-ups. The name comes from a line in Lost Mind, a song by Percy Mayfield from 1951 that Mose Allison recorded in 1957. Brood and his manager Koos van Dijk were fans of Allison. The best-known line-up played from November 1977 to October 1979 with Dany Lademacher on guitar, Fred van Kampen on bass, Kees Meerman on drums and two backing singers, the Bombita's.

The band was called a new wave band, although the head of the record company Ariola disputed that label when promoting it in America in 1979. He felt it had come about because Brood was a European artist. American record reviews of the time compared the record with Bruce Springsteen and Graham Parker. The album Go Nutz, produced by Tim O'Brien, contained rhythm-and-blues-flavoured rock and versions of I'll Be Doggone and Beauty Is Only Skin Deep.

Brood released many albums in the 1970s and 1980s, including Street, Shpritsz and Frisz & Sympatisz. After the line-up of 1977 to 1979 the success was not repeated. The music is raw, direct rock with a lot of piano, and Brood, like Golden Earring, chose English. In the Nederpop of School of Rock, Wild Romance is the band behind Saturday Night from 1978.
artiest/wild-romance.listen: Listen to Saturday Night by Herman Brood & His Wild Romance. Notice the piano and the raw vocals, and how the band keeps the song tight and fast.

artiest/wildstylez.text:
Wildstylez is the stage name of Joram Metekohy, a Dutch hardstyle DJ and producer, born in 1983. In 2004 he began producing hardstyle under the name Seizure, together with Ruben Hooyer, and released records on labels such as Sys-X, Blutonium and Scantraxx. At the end of 2007 his first solo release as Wildstylez appeared, on Headhunterz's Scantraxx sublabel. In 2008 he formed the duo Project One with Headhunterz, who made an album of thirteen tracks in less than three months. The album was released on 25 July 2008, shortly after their first performance at Defqon.1.

In 2009 came Tonight, a collaboration between Headhunterz and Wildstylez with Noisecontrollers, which came second in the Q-dance Harder Styles top 1000 in 2013. With Noisecontrollers he founded the label Digital:Age in 2010, and in 2013 followed his own label Lose Control Music. In 2012 Year of Summer, with the singer Niels Geusebroek, brought him into the Dutch popular dance scene. Timeless, which premiered at the Defqon.1 Endshow in 2012, became one of the best-known hardstyle tracks. His first solo album Lose Control was released in 2015.

Wildstylez makes emotional, melodic hardstyle and also works with mainstream DJs. With Hardwell he made Shine A Light in 2018, and in 2022 Typically Dutch was released with Armin van Buuren. In 2018 he founded the label Art of Creation with Headhunterz. In 2023 Year of Summer became the first hardstyle track in the Top 2000 of NPO Radio 2. His work shows how hardstyle grew from the Dutch club scene into something that crossed borders.
artiest/wildstylez.listen: Listen to Year of Summer and notice Niels Geusebroek's vocals and the stomping kick beneath them. Can you hear how a hardstyle track is given a melody that also fits on the radio?

artiest/wiley.text:
Wiley, born Richard Cowie Jr. in 1979 in Bow, in the east of London, is often called the Godfather of Grime. His father was a reggae artist and introduced him to drums and to early hip hop. He started out as a DJ, then moved on to rapping, and played his own productions on pirate radio stations such as Rinse FM. In UK garage he had success with the crews Ladies Hit Squad and Pay As U Go, who had a hit with Champagne Dance in 2002. He then founded Roll Deep, a group that also included Dizzee Rascal and Tinchy Stryder, which broke away from the garage sound and eventually became grime.

From 2001 Wiley released instrumental singles on his own label, including Eskimo, Avalanche and Ice Rink. His debut album Treddin' on Thin Ice was released in 2004 on XL Recordings. It included Wot Do U Call It?, a song that asked what name belonged to his music. Hits such as Wearing My Rolex and Heatwave followed later, and in 2017 the album Godfather.

Grime is hard, fast and angular, with short, digital sounds and rap in a hectic rhythm. Wiley used the Korg Triton on Wot Do U Call It?, and as a result that synthesizer became a fixture of the genre. He laid the foundation for a British style that grew independently of American hip hop.
artiest/wiley.listen: Listen to Wot Do U Call It? and notice the synthesizer sound and the angular beat. Can you hear how the question in the title returns in the lyrics?

artiest/wilfrido-vargas.text:
Wilfrido Vargas was born in the Dominican Republic in 1949 and grew up surrounded by music: his father played accordion and guitar, his mother flute and guitar. At the age of ten he went to the municipal music academy. He recorded his first album in 1972 with his band Wilfrido Vargas y sus Beduinos. In 1976 they played at Madison Square Garden, and in 1978 El Barbarazo came out, his first international hit. In 1979 he performed at the Havana Jam festival, together with the Fania All-Stars.

In the 1980s he founded and led several successful merengue groups, including Las Chicas del Can and The New York Band. International success came with El Jardinero, La Medicina, El Africano and El Loco y La Luna. El Africano, from the 1983 album El funcionario, became the basis for Mami El Negro by the rapper DJ Laz. In 1991 he was nominated for a Grammy. In 1993 the Dominican president awarded him the Order of Christopher Columbus for his contribution to spreading the national music.

Merengue is the fast Dominican dance music with accordion or brass, tambora and güira. Vargas played an important part in making the style known worldwide. He was a composer, arranger and bandleader, and made merengue heard in discos far beyond the Caribbean. He now lives in Colombia.
artiest/wilfrido-vargas.listen: Listen to El Jardinero and notice the lightning-fast rhythm and the brass. Can you hear how the song never stands still, so that you almost have to dance along?

artiest/wilhelm-furtwangler.text:
Wilhelm Furtwängler was born in Schöneberg near Berlin in 1886, the son of an archaeologist and a painter. He grew up in Munich and received music lessons from an early age. His love was for Beethoven. He saw himself first and foremost as a composer and began conducting in order to perform his own work. He made his debut with Bruckner's Ninth Symphony. After that he worked in, among other places, Munich, Strasbourg, Lübeck, Mannheim, Frankfurt and Vienna. In 1920 he succeeded Richard Strauss at the Berlin Staatskapelle, and in 1922 he became principal conductor of the Gewandhaus Orchestra in Leipzig and of the Berlin Philharmonic. He remained with the latter orchestra until 1945 and again from 1952 to 1954.

Furtwängler is regarded as one of the greatest symphonic and opera conductors of the twentieth century. He also conducted a great deal with the Wiener Philharmoniker. His recordings are well known, including the Eroica and Beethoven's Ninth, Tristan und Isolde, Die Walküre and Schubert's Seventh. Many later conductors refer to his style of interpretation. His own compositions, including the Second Symphony, found less response.

During the Nazi regime he remained Germany's foremost conductor. He never became a member of the party, refused the Hitler salute and wrote an open letter against antisemitism in music in 1933. Even so, it remained a sensitive matter that his presence lent the regime prestige. In January 1945 he fled to Switzerland. After the war he conducted again, and he died in 1954 near Baden-Baden. Furtwängler stands for the heavy, Romantic German tradition in conducting, and for the question of how an artist conducts himself under a dictatorship.
artiest/wilhelm-furtwangler.listen: Listen to his 1952 recording of the Eroica and notice the changes of tempo and the tension in the slow march. Can you hear how freely he lets the tempo move within a single movement?

artiest/will-marion-cook.text:
Will Marion Cook was born in Washington, D.C., in 1869 as William Mercer Cook. His father was one of the first Black lawyers in the city. He studied violin at the Oberlin conservatory and, from 1887 to 1889, at the Berlin Hochschule für Musik. In 1894 and 1895 he was taught by Antonín Dvořák in New York. Because of the strict segregation in classical music, his career as a soloist did not take off, and he found a home in musical theatre.

In 1898 his one-act piece Clorindy, or The Origin of the Cake Walk came about, with lyrics by the poet Paul Laurence Dunbar. In 1903 followed In Dahomey, with the comedians Bert Williams and George Walker in the leading roles. It is regarded as the first full-length musical by and for Black creators in a major Broadway theatre. In Dahomey toured for four years, including in the United Kingdom and the United States. Cook was composer and musical director of the Williams and Walker company and also wrote Abyssinia in 1906 and Bandanna Land in 1907. His songs used folk music in a way of their own.

In 1918 and 1919 he travelled with his New York Syncopated Orchestra, also called the Southern Syncopated Orchestra, to England, where it played for King George V. The clarinettist Sidney Bechet played in that orchestra. Cook also gave advice to younger musicians such as Eubie Blake and Duke Ellington. He died in New York in 1944. Cook joined European training with African American music and showed that Black creators could define the theatre.
artiest/will-marion-cook.listen: Listen to a recording of a number from In Dahomey or Clorindy and notice the syncopated rhythm that comes from the cakewalk. Can you hear how the rhythm makes the melody danceable?

artiest/will-young.text:
Will Young is an English singer, songwriter and actor, born in Wokingham, Berkshire, in 1979. He grew up in Hungerford, became head chorister at school and learned to play the piano at the age of nine. He studied politics at the University of Exeter and played in a theatre group, where he got the role of Curly in Oklahoma! After that he trained in musical theatre in London. In 1999 he had already auditioned for a boy band on the TV programme This Morning, but that group had no success.

In 2001 he entered Pop Idol, a talent show on ITV. In a preliminary round he sang a jazzy, lounge-style version of Light My Fire by The Doors. The judge Simon Cowell called it average, but the public voted Young through as number one. The incident is often seen as the start of his pop career. In 2002 he won the first Idol competition in the world. His double debut single Anything Is Possible and Evergreen became the fastest-selling debut single in Britain.

His debut album From Now On from 2002 went straight to number one. Friday's Child from 2003 did even better. Keep On, Let It Go, Echoes, 85% Proof, Lexicon and Crying on the Bathroom Floor followed. He also acted in film and theatre, including in Mrs. Henderson Presents in 2005 and in the musical Cabaret in London, for which he received an Olivier nomination. He has also written books, including the autobiography Funny Peculiar. Young showed that a television contest could lead to a lasting career.
artiest/will-young.listen: Listen to his version of Light My Fire and notice how calmly and smoothly he sings the song by The Doors. What is left of the original?

artiest/willem-breuker.text: The saxophonist and composer Willem Breuker, from Amsterdam, played on Peter Brötzmann's Machine Gun in 1968. With Misha Mengelberg and Han Bennink he founded the Instant Composers Pool in 1967, but he soon went his own way. In 1974 he started the Willem Breuker Kollektief, a group of about ten musicians that mixed jazz with marches, tango, Kurt Weill, brass band music and classical music. The performances were theatrical and full of humour. Breuker was also active in the fight for subsidies for improvised music and helped found the Bimhuis. He wrote a great deal of music for theatre and film. He died in 2010.
artiest/willem-breuker.listen: Notice the unexpected changes of style: a tango, a march, then free jazz again.

artiest/willem-breuker-kollektief.text:
The Willem Breuker Kollektief was a Dutch ten-piece jazz orchestra, founded in 1974 by the saxophonist and clarinettist Willem Breuker. Breuker, born in 1944, played in the 1960s with the percussionist Han Bennink and the pianist Misha Mengelberg and founded the Instant Composers Pool with them. He was also a member of the Globe Unity Orchestra and of Gunter Hampel's group. With his own Kollektief he chose a different path: jazz that was theatrical and often unconventional, with elements from theatre and vaudeville.

The group toured Western Europe, Russia, Australia, India, China, Japan, the United States and Canada. In 1974 Breuker founded the record label BV Haast, on which many of the Kollektief's albums appeared, such as W.B.K. '79 from 1979, Driebergen-Zeist from 1983, Bob's Gallery from 1988 and Metropolis from 1990. From 1977 he organised the annual festival Klap op de Vuurpijl in Amsterdam, and his publishing house Haast published his scores. In 1999 the book Willem Breuker Kollektief: Celebrating 25 Years on the Road appeared, with two albums.

In 1997 Breuker also produced a forty-eight-hour radio documentary about Kurt Weill. In 1998 he was made a Knight of the Order of the Netherlands Lion. He died in Amsterdam in 2010, and since 2017 the Willem Breuker Prize for contemporary composers has existed. The Kollektief showed that Dutch jazz could be spectacular, humorous and yet musically serious.
artiest/willem-breuker-kollektief.listen: Listen to a recording by the Willem Breuker Kollektief, for example from the album Bob's Gallery, and notice the sudden changes of style. Can you hear how a number can leap from swing to circus music or a march?

artiest/willem-ix-van-aquitanie.text:
William IX of Aquitaine, in Occitan Guilhèm de Peitieus, was born in 1071 and was Duke of Aquitaine and Gascony and Count of Poitou from 1086 until his death in 1126. He inherited the duchy from his father at the age of fifteen. His life was full of conflict: he was excommunicated twice, the second time because he abducted the viscountess Dangereuse and had her live in his castle in Poitiers. In 1101 he took part in a crusade, which ended badly for him: his army was destroyed and he himself escaped with a handful of men. Between 1120 and 1123 he fought in Spain, together with Castile and León.

His lasting significance lies in poetry. William IX is the earliest troubadour whose work has survived: a poet who wrote in Occitan, the vernacular of southern France. Eleven songs are known. They deal with love, sex, women, his own prowess and feudal politics. A medieval biography calls him one of the most courtly men in the world and a great seducer. The songs have a frank, comic tone and shocked and charmed at the same time.

The song Pos de chantar m'es pres talenz is a meditation on mortality, possibly written around the time of his first excommunication. The epithet the Troubadour was only given to him in the nineteenth century. His granddaughter Eleanor of Aquitaine inherited his court. As the first love poet in the vernacular, William IX opened a tradition that later led to Dante, Petrarch and Villon, and even reached poets such as Ezra Pound.
artiest/willem-ix-van-aquitanie.listen: Listen to a recording of Pos de chantar m'es pres talenz on the album Las Cansos del Coms de Peitieus and notice the simple melody and the accompaniment on old instruments. Can you hear how the text and a single singing voice take centre stage?
